text: Welcome to another Japan vlog!
This suitcase is about to fall apart
Today our first stop is Tokyo
We'll be exploring southern Hokkaido by air
Thank you to Japan Airlines for taking us on this journey!
This is JAL SKY SUITE III in Business Class
The seats come with a massage function 😂
Nice amenities like slippers and eye masks
Free Wi-Fi for Business Class
But I'm most looking forward to the Japanese meal service
The prettiest inflight meal I've ever seen
Watching my favourite movie, Shaolin Soccer
Ending the flight with a sake tasting
How do I describe the euphoric feeling of walking through Haneda Airport 😂
This time last year it was 38℃ (100.4°F)
Bracing ourselves...
Honestly it's really nice for early July!
Victor: we are home!
We're back where it all started at Tokyu Stay Ginza
It feels like a full circle moment staying at this hotel in Tokyo
If you guys watched our very first Tokyo vlog back in like 2022,
We stayed here for like over a month
And it's good to be back at this hotel for 1 night
Tomorrow we'll be heading to Sapporo!
It just so happens our friends are also in town, so we're grabbing a drink!
(We just saw them yesterday at the gym 😂)
A bar that reminds me of Potato Head in Bali 😂
With over 3,000 vinyl records
Very foreigner friendly
Love the Japanese city pop playlist
The vibes are immaculate, the cocktails are ok
An early start to the airport
Ginza to Haneda Airport is around 25 minutes by taxi
Today we'll be heading to Hokkaido by airplane
Japan Airlines' dedicated domestic First Class check-in counter
Check-in within 5 minutes through a private security lane
Popping into the lounge for a bite
Is it too early for a beer? 😅
We love watching the crew wave goodbye to travellers
Japan Airlines' new domestic First Class cabin seats
The flight is only 1.5 hours long
Complimentary seasonal meal service
The staff offered to help each guest take a photo
I love how they showcase Japan by using local ingredients
A cute handwritten note from the staff!
We were just here back in March
It's our third time in Hokkaido for the summer where the weather is perfect
We just arrived at Sapporo Station and now we're going to stay right across!
Trying a new hotel today!
This hotel is great if you plan to stay in the winter
Our room isn't ready yet so we'll go out for lunch
The hotel is connected to the underground tunnel that leads to Sapporo Station
Lavender lines all the streets of Sapporo
This is a very interesting location for a famous ramen shop
It feels like the Toronto suburbs
A ramen shop located inside a wholesale seafood market
Coffee on the right, ramen on the left
Next door is a coffee shop
Sam is queuing for ramen so I'll get a quick coffee
Drinking this quickly because I can't bring it into the ramen shop
Nouilles is listed on Tabelog's "Ramen HOKKAIDO Top 100 Restaurants"
The ramen infuses French and Italian cooking techniques
The space is elegant and refined
The clear broth is a French consommé style using local chicken and pork
The broth isn't heavy and rich but it's perfect for the summer
The ramen is topped with its famous kelp foam
The noodles are paired with sous-vide duck and charcoal-grilled chicken
Perhaps this is the most elegant bowl of ramen I've ever eaten!
On our way to a cafe, we stumbled upon a neighbourhood festival
You know you're in Hokkaido when you see crab legs casually being grilled
A cafe located upstairs
This is true!
Eccentric retro style interiors

This one is layered with soft cream, cornflakes,
 coffee jelly and topped with a whole pudding!
You can't go to Hokkaido without experiencing the night parfait culture
Many people go to Hokkaido for skiing in the winter
But if you want to experience a cool summer, Hokkaido is the best!
A beautiful little shrine with decorations that change with the season
For summer, the theme is marine blue and white
Cute glass jellyfish wind chimes
The flower washing basin is also stunning
The shrine is about a 15 minute walk from Sapporo Station
We'll head back to the hotel to check-in first
This is the Essential Double room
This hotel opened in December 2025 so it feels very new
Open-layout bathroom
Standing shower and bathtub
Our room faces Sapporo Station and Daimaru
We'll spend the rest of the evening walking around the malls
Please watch our previous Hokkaido vlogs if you want in-depth shop introductions!
We will leave all the names of the shops on the top right
Tried on a few new tops for the summer
These are a few of my go-to homeware shops in Sapporo Station:
I usually come here to buy souvenirs but we'll just get a soft cream this time
A soup curry joint we always go to
While we eat, here's a few photos from Sapporo!
Time for bed because we have a flight to catch in the morning!
Another early morning to the local airport
It'll take 20 minutes to reach the airport
Okadama is Sapporo's domestic airport
We'll be flying with Hokkaido Air System (HAC) today!
It's the regional JAL group airline that flies with propeller-type airplanes
The plane has its own merch
They also fly to other parts of Hokkaido like Rishiri, Kushiro and Memanbetsu
It feels like I'm flying a private jet 😂
The staff hand out candy with a sweet note
Wow you can see the famous star-shaped Goryokaku Park from above!
A stained glass window with Hakodate motifs
Like many of the Hoshino hotels, OMO5 Hakodate has an onsen
(We got permission to film when the onsen was closed for cleaning 🙏🏼)
The male and female onsen spaces are mirror images of each other
The bathhouse uses only natural hot spring water
The water is brownish-red because it's high in sodium and iron
We booked the "View Bath Twin Room with sofa bed"
The bathtub has a view overlooking the bay
From our balcony we can see the JR train station
I'm starving! Let's grab lunch at the Morning Market nearby
If you visit on the weekends, you can catch the vintage trams
The market is a 5 minute walk from our hotel
If you watched our last summer in Hokkaido vlog, this restaurant may sound familiar
We visited their Otaru branch last year!
Uni Murakami specialises in 100% additive free sea urchin
The summer is the best time to eat sea urchin in Hakodate
You can try Bafun uni here which is rich and creamy
By the time we finished lunch, most of the shops in the area were already closed
A seafood lover's paradise
We'll come back another morning to shop around
We'll slowly walk over to the famous red brick warehouses
A charming waterfront complex full of souvenir shops and cafes
We'll come back on our last day!
The architecture in Hakodate is really cool
You will see many Japanese-Western hybrid buildings
A beautiful teahouse located in a historical earthen storehouse
The interiors are a blend of Western Japanese styles
The second floor is closed since the cafe is empty
But the owner was kind enough to allow me to take a look
Upstairs is traditional tatami seating
A small roastery where they play jazz while making coffee
Music-inspired coffee blends
We're entering the church district
It's foggy today so it's not ideal for going up Mt. Hakodate
Motomachi is a neighbourhood where East meets West
When Japan opened for international trade,
Many missionaries built churches in the area
These are the famous churches in Hakodate all in one area
And the iconic slope road
The Anglican Hakodate St. John's Church
The Orthodox Church sits next door
The Catholic Church
You'll find cobblestone streets and colonial style houses
A colonial style house that has a panoramic view of the city below
There isn't a whole lot to see in every room but you can get a taste of the architecture
And learn about Japanese-Western hybrid buildings that are unique to Hakodate
Squat toilet!
The grand ballroom with a terrace where you can admire the view
Waiting for the bus to go home!
Heading back to the hotel for a drink
Hakodate is home to 20 churches
As an ode to the churches,
The hotel plays a fully restored hand-crank organ
This organ was once used at Goryokaku Tower
The lounge is decorated in stained glass lamps as an homage to the churches
Recommended after day of sightseeing or enjoying the onsen!
Checking out the map to see what restaurants are around
Lucky Pierrot is a local-only fast food chain restaurant
Be ready to be overstimulated
There are 17 shops: the owner doesn't plan to expand beyond Hakodate
Me trying to find the English menu 🔎🔎🔎
A huge souvenir corner
The fast food chain's owner is an ethnic-Chinese Japanese
The most popular dish is the "Chinese Chicken Burger"
Everything feels very analog here including the menus and payment system (cash only)
No two Lucky Pierrot interiors are the same
Each has a theme: ours is "I Love Matisse’s Red" (マティスの赤が好き)"
The owner was inspired by the energy of the Morning Market nearby
It reminds me of a vintage McDonald's
The portions are huge and extremely cheap
They also have Japanese dishes like omurice and oyakodon
All this is ¥2,222 (USD 14)
Sweet and sour chicken chunks
With so much fresh seafood available in Hakodate,
This was a one-time experience for me personally!
But I love the nostalgic interiors
We have a late night dessert courtesy of FamilyMart
I picked up the Morinaga 40th Anniversary Limited Edition milk ice bar
With chocolate bits in it!
And I have the FamilyMart Cookies & Cream popsicle
From Hokkaido milk
Mine looks like a zebra!
Mine's half gone
If you like the Dairy Queen chocolate dip cone, you will like this
Because it's got a lot of chocolate crunchy bits woven into the vanilla ice cream
So it's got this fun textural contrast
Let's have a Hakodate-theme breakfast
A nod to Goryokaku fort with the star-shaped breakfast buffet
Build your own seafood bowl
They also have "ika-meshi"- a Southern Hokkaido specialty
Sushi and shio ramen is also available
Charcoal-grilled vegetables, squid and salmon
They also have a selection of Western breakfast items too
Marine-themed dining room
Squid stuffed with sticky rice
This morning we are going on a morning market tour with a guide!
It's conducted in Japanese

But we tried to use Google Live Translate 
to understand as much as possible
This market is said to be less touristy than the Hakodate Morning Market
It's frequented by locals and the prices are lower
There are around 40 shops here
The guide is introducing some of the vendors to our group
He said the tuna from Hakodate is just as good as the prized tuna from Aomori
The two cities sit on the Tsugaru Strait so they both catch tuna in same body of water
But it's a lot cheaper to buy Hakodate tuna!
The older I get, the more grocery shopping excites me
The atmosphere is very local
You can purchase small platters of sashimi and fresh fish roe
There are less souvenir-style shops here
But you can experience a slice of daily life
Besides fresh seafood, there's also stalls that sell smoked fish
We stop by a seaweed shop
I'm very excited because buying kombu in Hokkaido is on my shopping list 😂
We cook most of our meals at home in Hong Kong,
So we like to use kombu and seasonings to enhance the flavour
We end the tour by trying a few samples
We have Hakodate salmon, dashi, seaweed, crab and fish roe
Our tour is over but we'll stay behind to buy some fruit and seafood
Since we won't be visiting Furano this time, we will get some melon here!
I don't like the summer heat, but the fruit is undeniably the best this season
I'm back at the first fish vendor
I asked them to prepare it to eat as sashimi for tonight
Our tour guide also recommended this kaisendon cafe
Yes they serve seafood bowls and coffee (the best combo)
The famous Kiyoshi Kimura
Got my kombu, got my iced coffee
Our mini grocery haul
A sloped road that gently disappears into the sea
It's been featured in many Japanese anime, commercials and dramas
It's best to photograph the road on a clear day when the water is blue
Victor found the cutest teahouse by the seaside
They're open on Google Maps but in person they're closed 😫
I'm so sad because this tea shop looks so charming
It used to be a quarantine facility in the 1800's
And restored by locals
We went around to the back of the house
All these tables face the window with a view of the sea
It is one of the oldest Western style houses in Hakodate
And there's a beautiful garden full of hydrangeas
The Type A in me is thinking of a back-up plan 🧐
This is our back-up plan because Yūhi Teahouse was a total fail
This is Rokkatei
They're really famous for their sea views and cake
But I anticipate there's going to be a really long line
Because there's a lot of tourists who go to this location
Alright, let's predict the queue
I say 1.5 hours
Yeah right!
On the ground floor is the gift shop where you can buy their classic sweets
The view of the ocean is so distracting though
Get a ticket to queue for a table for the cafe
You can go up once your number is called
Today we got lucky!
The airport is nearby
To order a cake for dine-in, you need to go back to the gift shop
This view makes up for Tea Shop Yūhi
It looks like an American Klondike ice cream sandwich
But it's cheesecake sandwiched between 2 chocolate biscuits
Since it was lunchtime, we ordered a couple savoury dishes
On our way to Goryokaku Park
But we can't help but stop to check out the beaches
He didn't want to come down to the beach with me
Goryokaku Fort was the first Western-style fortress in Japan
It's also a famous cherry blossom spot where the sakura trees line the star-shaped fort
At the center of the fort is the Magistrate's Office

This is a reproduction; 
the original one was torn down to symbolise the end of the samurai
The clay roof tiles are so pretty
But we already have plans to go up the Goryokaku Tower next door
Here you can see the star shaped fortress from above
The Magistrate's Office from above
Next door is another Rokkatei
This is a garden-themed cafe
Stunning views of the cherry blossom trees
The cafe isn't as picturesque as the Isaribidori branch
Off to return the car and grab a beer!
We are back at the Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse for a drink and some shopping
A beautiful lofted ceiling brewery that reminds me of Harry Potter haha
We're going to grab a quick drink and a light snack before dinner
At the centre is a huge fireplace and cypress pillars
We will try some local beer
We are having soup curry with squid tonight!
This restaurant was recommended by the hotel
Hakodate style soup curry
When in Hakodate, we have to try squid in every dish
The squid curry includes squid rings, legs, scallop and seaweed
We made reservations to take the hotel bus up Mt.Hakodate
Cars are restricted at certain times to go up Mt. Hakodate,
So we are taking our hotel's shuttle bus up to see the night time view!
Depending on the season, private cars aren't allowed up starting at 4-5pm
Everyone is here to see Hakodate's "Million Dollar View"
To highlight the hourglass shape of the city,
Warm orange lights are installed
While cool white lamps are used in the fishing ports
The city intentionally banned large neon billboards
And has building height restrictions to avoid obstructing the waves of light
There's also a small cafe if it's too windy outside
So for today's midnight snack
We have a variety of produce from the morning market
First we have a little tray of sea urchin
And 2 types of tuna
Normally, we eat the sea urchin with rice and seaweed
But since we don't have any of that
I suddenly came up with the idea of pairing it with potato chips
Either this will be a really good trend that we just started
Or we'll have wasted some good uni on these chips
Let's try it out!
That's some good uni though!
I think I'm going to just eat the uni by itself
Because the uni itself is really good
Victor: I'll have chips by itself
Ok, I'm going to try this natural tuna
Off to the onsen! Goodnight!
It's coffee time!
This cafe is only a 6 minute walk from the hotel
When I saw the train-inspired facade and the cute interior,
I knew we had to visit!
The owner told us to write down our order (is he trolling us 😂)
How's our handwriting? 😂
The shop is run by one man
Yum I love a thick buttery toast
Smoking is allowed inside
The morning market is located next to the JR train station and the port
Serving locals post WWII who were suffering from food shortages
Now it's a tourist attraction especially for foodies
You can eat fresh sea urchin or have a crab cooked in front of you
Food court style setting so you can eat immediately!
If you're not into seafood, they also have stalls selling seasonings and fruit
As for me, I'm on the hunt for a specific type of sea urchin
Victor loves salmon roe so we stopped by this ikura shop
They sell ikura by the bottle
We got a vial of fish roe eggs that Victor's going to eat straight out of the jar
The fish roe is pickled in soy sauce
Next to our table, Victor spotted this lady selling seaweed
He said he wanted to support her

We told her to keep the change since she didn't have exact,
but insisted on giving us a ¥50 discount
I finally found a shop selling the sea urchin
They will ask you when you plan on eating it so they can pack accordingly
I asked them how long it can last for and they said 2 days
We wanted to try the "Ika Odori Don" aka Dancing Squid Bowl
But this restaurant, Tabiji, already sold out
It was featured on many local tv shows
The coolest thing about Hakodate are the unique Western-Japanese buildings
Many houses feature a Japanese first floor and a European style second floor
This is a vintage shop that is also housed in a Western-Japanese building
Unfortunately you can't take photos inside but they have a lot of vintage homeware!
This is our first espresso-based coffee on this whole trip
Currently they're only doing takeaway drinks
A hybrid design studio/cafe/bar/shop
Wow perfect light roast coffee! Sadly they don't sell beans
A sweets shop that's famous for its crepes and chocolate truffles
Oh no, the strawberry crepe is sold out 😭
Each crepe is made to order
Totally ordered the wrong thing,
I got coffee jelly instead of a crepe
I thought it was coffee jelly in a crepe
This is more like a sundae with creme anglaise and vanilla ice cream
A matcha shop just around the corner from Hachimanzaka Slope
This counter was made just for people to take pictures
They also offer hojicha!
They're actually a real estate company with a matcha pop-up in the front
We got our matcha cream lattes and we're going to sit by the harbour
Let's check out the brick warehouses!
A glasswork shop
It reminds me of the shops in Otaru
Many shops sell knick knacks and snacks
Since it's summer, we'll go see if the hydrangeas are in bloom
The blue hydrangea have fully bloomed
But the white varieties still need a few more weeks
Stopping by a women's convent that is nearby
An active monastery that was opened by 8 French nuns
You aren't allowed inside so we will quickly tour the grounds
But it's not worth going out of your way here
Back in the city for our last dinner
A famous ramen shop known for its Hakodate shio ramen
It was originally a Chinese restaurant
Personally the broth was a little too salty for me
Here's some photos of Hakodate from our last day!
We're back with another Hakodate midnight snack
featuring some preservative-free fresh uni!
We "uni" eat uni in Hakodate!
Here it is!:
The packaging is slightly different because it comes in 2 layers
And the sea urchin is just floating in sea salt water
